mappings.note: Contrasts wind-built dunes with collision-built mountains - two formation agents, which is exactly LO-2. Not C-SST1.1, because both landforms are already named and only the process separates the options.

A term-and-definition matching item over subcontinent, tributary, plateau and monsoon - geographical vocabulary under the describe competency. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, since the monsoon option is a wrong distractor and nothing is located.

Wide plains, deltas and Chilika lagoon have to be resolved to the East Coast - identification from relief and coastal landforms. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because no climatic criterion appears in the clue set.
Finds the false river-source pairing (Brahmaputra from the Thar). Identification of where rivers rise, so the describe-landforms competency; not C-SST1.1-LO-2, since no formation process is at stake.
The reason fails because an eastward tilt sends the Deccan rivers east, not west - a description of the plateau's slope and drainage. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2: the tilt is given, its origin is never asked.

All three statements are about origins - young fold mountains still rising, an ancient stable plateau, and plains of alluvium rather than lava. That makes it a formation item, not the bare C-SST1.1 description.
The Sundarbans as the refuge of the endangered Royal Bengal Tiger sits in the flora-and-fauna conservation lane. Not C-SST1.1, because the delta is only the setting and the answer is a species.
Infers clear, warm, shallow water from the presence of coral reefs, i.e. the conditions under which coral islands are built. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3, because nothing about protecting the reef is asked.

The answer is that India's diverse regions were tied together by internal trade routes carrying goods and ideas - geography shaping how people lived and exchanged. Not CG-SST2, whose history goal in this frame covers medieval kingdoms, temples and bhakti, none of which the item touches.
India's rank by area is a fact about its extent on the world map, which is the only outcome about distribution and extent. Not C-SST1.1, because no landform is described.
Naming a neighbour inside the Indian Subcontinent is placing countries on the world map. Not C-SST1.1: a country is not a landform, so the describe-landforms competency would be the wrong lane.
Recall that the Himalayas form India's northern barrier - identification of a landform and its role. Part of the chapter's large factual-recall block that this frame can only serve through C-SST1.1.
The meaning of 'hima' is the descriptive vocabulary of the snow-covered range. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because snow here is part of a name, not a climatic region being located.
The 2,500 km length of the range is a dimension of a landform. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, since the extent asked for is of a mountain chain, not of a climatic region.
Names the Himadri as the highest Himalayan belt - relief identification. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because height rather than climate is the criterion.
Recall of a hill station in the Lower Himalayas - a placement fact within a named range. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because why hill stations sit in that belt is not asked, only a name.
Identifies the Shivaliks as the outermost and lowest range - relief description. Sibling C-SST1.1-LO-2 is wrong because the item never touches how the foothills were raised.
Source of the Bhagirathi at Gaumukh - identification of a river's origin. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2: no glacial process is required, just the place.
Which glacier Gaumukh sits at the edge of - again a named-feature recall. Distinct from the Bhagirathi item only in what is being named; the frame offers no narrower outcome for either.
'Tso' as the Ladakhi word for lake is water-body vocabulary under the describe competency. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because the cultural angle is incidental and no way of life is examined.
Recall that 'moonland' means Ladakh, keyed on terrain appearance. Deliberately not C-SST1.1-LO-2, which was used for the companion item that asks how that folded terrain came about.
Names a river system feeding the Northern Plains - drainage identification. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because the plain's alluvial build-up is handled by other items in this chapter.
The Great Indian Desert is the arid region of the country, so naming it is placing a climatic region. Not C-SST1.1, because a desert is defined by rainfall rather than relief.
Names a state the Thar covers - the extent of an arid region on the map, which is precisely LO-1. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, since no aspect of desert life is asked.

Taanka and kund as rainwater harvesting keeps this in the water-conservation lane with the other harvesting items. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because the structure exists to save a scarce resource, not merely to illustrate desert living.
Identifies the Aravallis as among the world's oldest ranges. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2: the companion assertion-reason item tests how they were folded, this one only asks which hills they are.
Definition of 'peninsula' as a landform term. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, since no place has to be located.
Names the Western Ghats as the plateau's western rim - relief identification. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because the Ghats are asked as a boundary range, not as a rainfall divide.
Recall of 'Sahyadri' for the northern Western Ghats. A short-answer twin of the earlier MCQ on the same fact; both sit on C-SST1.1 because the frame has no finer outcome for Indian relief names.
Names an east-flowing peninsular river - drainage identification. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, because the plateau's tilt is not what has to be explained here.
Names a west-flowing river (Narmada or Tapti), the counterpart to the east-flowing item. Same competency for the same reason: it is a named-feature recall with no process or climate content.
Identifies Lakshadweep as the Arabian Sea group. Not C-SST1.2-LO-1, because the pairing is recalled rather than read off a map or globe.
Names Barren Island as India's only active volcano - feature identification. Not C-SST1.1-LO-2, since volcanic landform building is not part of the answer.

Explaining the Indian Subcontinent means giving its reach across India and its neighbours, i.e. the extent of a region on the world map. Not C-SST1.1, because countries rather than landforms make up the answer.

'Water Tower of Asia' is justified by snowmelt supplying water to millions downstream - the mountain-to-livelihood link. Not CG-SST1, because the specific LO carries the environment-and-people relationship already.
Asks outright how the Himalayas were formed - break-up of Gondwana, northward drift, collision and crumpling. The clearest LO-2 item in the chapter; C-SST1.1 alone would understate it.

Requires the Himadri's position and its year-round snow cover, so a climatic belt is being described as well as located. Not C-SST1.2-LO-2, because the answer stops at 'life is tough' and does not work out how people live there.

The Shivaliks' significance as the lowest range and the transition to the plains is a relief-and-position description. Not C-SST1.3-LO-3, even though wildlife is mentioned, since conservation is never raised.
